The Delinquency Score predicts the likelihood that your business will pay its bills
on time in the future based on information in the Dun & Bradstreet Data Cloud.
Your Delinquency Score comes in three flavors; a Class, a Percentile and a Raw
Score – allowing for different levels of granularity.
To creditors, suppliers and other businesses, your Delinquency Score can help
measure if your business will pay on time.
Your Delinquency Score can change over time

Raw Score: D&B calculates a “raw” score to predict the likelihood that your business will not pay its bills on time.
Class: D&B applies a “class” to categorize your business according to a level of risk.
Probability of Delinquency: This indicates the probability that your business will pay its bills after they are due.
Industry Avg. Probability of Delinquency: This is your industry’s benchmark that a business will pay its bills after they are due.

The Failure Score predicts the likelihood that a company will declare bankruptcy or
close its doors in the next 12 months. Your Failure Score comes in three flavors; a
Class, a Percentile and a Raw Score – allowing for different levels of granularity.
To creditors, vendors, suppliers and other businesses, your Failure Score measures
their risk of loss associated with doing business with your business.
Your Failure Score can change over time
These factors are affecting your score:
Limited time under present management control
Raw Score: D&B calculates a “raw” score to predict the likelihood that your business will no longer be in business or declare bankruptcy in the next 12 months.
Class: D&B applies a “class” to categorize your business according to the level of risk associated with your business.
Probability of Failure: This indicates the probability that your business will go out of business or declare bankruptcy in the next 12 months.
Industry Avg. Probability of Failure: This is your industry’s benchmark that a business will go out of business or declare bankruptcy in the next 12 months.

The D&B Supplier Evaluation Risk (SER) Rating predicts the likelihood that a
supplier will cease operations or become inactive over the next 12 months based
on information in the Dun & Bradstreet Data Cloud. Using statistical probability
factors, it scores public and private companies from 1 to 9, where 1 represents low
risk and 9 represents high risk. The SER Rating provides powerful supplier insight
by combining key risk indicators into a single rating.

D&B Rating is an indicator typically used by financial institutions, vendors and
suppliers to help assess the creditworthiness of your business. Your D&B Rating is
determined by combining your business’s net worth and the summary of your
business’s financial health, payment habits and operational performance.

reaching a credit decision. Some reasons for using the "- -" symbol include: deficit net worth,
bankruptcy proceedings, lack of sufficient payment information or incomplete history
